correctness.rationale: I checked the geometry and recovered the arithmetic independently with python3 /workspace/audit_quartic.py. Smoothness can also be checked directly: on e1=0 the constrained partials agree only if all xi solve z^3+e2 z=constant, because the e2-square term has zero derivative. With two distinct values, the value of odd multiplicity is zero, and the patterns (4,1) and (2,3) fail the surface equation. With three distinct values a,b,c, their sum is zero and ab+ac+bc=e2; for multiplicities (3,1,1) this forces a=0 for the triple value, hence b=c, and for (2,2,1) the singleton is zero by e1=0 and the pair values again coincide. One value would give only the zero vector. Thus it is a smooth quartic K3. In a separate F4-to-F16 quadratic-tower implementation I enumerated normalized projective points, finding (20,554), and found all 60 F16-lines from pairs of these points (five distinct zeros force the binary quartic restriction to vanish). Their F4-Frobenius permutes them in 30 transpositions. Direct intersections and exact rational ranks give rank G=20 and rank G(I+P)=rank G(I-P)=10. The published rank-20 span gives the upper bound, and the intersection pairing identifies the two ranks with the two eigenspace dimensions. The two actions on untwisted H2 are therefore +4 and -4 with multiplicity ten each; inverting the permutation for geometric Frobenius has no effect. The 22-dimensional K3 trace formula then gives remaining traces 3 and -23 for F and F squared. Newton's identity gives product 16, hence residual factor X^2-3X+16 and discriminant -55. The H0 and H4 factors complete the stated zeta function in all extensions. No claim is made about other twists or the line complement.
